recipes.name: Fisherman’s Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 pound cod fillets, cut into chunks
1.5 cups warm milk, or more as needed
1 cup shredded sharp white Cheddar cheese
1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained
0.5 teaspoon ground black pepper, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Arrange cod in a single layer in a large baking dish; set aside.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Whisk in flour, and stir until the mixture becomes paste-like and light golden brown, 2 to 5 minutes.
Gradually whisk warm milk into the flour mixture and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Whisk until the sauce is thick and smooth, about 5 minutes.
Whisk in white Cheddar cheese, then mix onion, spinach, salt, and black pepper into the sauce.
Remove saucepan from heat and stir in garlic. If sauce is too thick, stir in more warm milk, 1 tablespoon at a time.
Pour sauce over fish in baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes, then sprinkle with yellow Cheddar cheese. Continue baking until fish is easily flaked with a fork, 15 to 20 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Fisherman’s Pie
raw_recipe.description: This cheesy casserole has moist chunks of fish in a rich white sauce and is a great way to use up leftover mashed potatoes.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe. Very tasty. I sliced my potatoes instead of mashing them. Turned out beautifully. I also added some shrimp and scallops too make it a bit special, but it isn't really necessary as the pie is so tasty even without the high cost additives. Whole family loved it.

My 99 year old FIL loves cod. He also has dysphagia. This recipe filled the bill for both - he ate 3 helpings! And he told me how good it was 4 or 5 times! 45 minutes is WAY too long to cook this. I did 30 minutes tonight and will probably go for 20 next time. I used 6 ounces of sliced fresh spinach and sautéed it down with the onion. Also, I used Bob Evans All Natural Mashed Potatoes to save time. Thanks for an excellent recipe!

We had just under 1.5lbs of cod and 12 oz. of fresh spinach. Cooked the spinach in just a little of the butter until wilted and the water cooked out. Then melted the rest of the butter and added the onion, cooking until soft. Added the flour, then also added a crushed clove of garlic, cooking until the flour started to brown. Needed about 2C of milk to make a nice sauce and added some thyme, parsley, black pepper and a dash of cayenne. Used a little less cheese than was called for in sauce and topping, and had about 5C of (leftover) mashed potatos for the top. Second helpings were in order!

I made it with peas instead of spinach. It turned out delicious! I'll definitely make this again! I also used a haberano cheese on top of the mashed potatoes instead of orange cheddar. And in addiction to baking 15 minutes with the cheese on top I also broiled it for a few minutes to get a nice golden crust. Thanks for the recipe :)

OK, but very bland. White fish, white sauce and mashed potato is a boring combination. I used frozen green beans and edamame (defrosted) instead of the spinach. Would have been better if had cooked onions and garlic in the butter before adding the rest of the sauce ingredients. I also think sliced potatoes would have been nicer - more of a scalloped potato style recipe with fish at the bottom. Yellow American cheddar (which for once I had on hand) is useless too. Better a good import - British or New Zealand. Or another cheese.

I cooked haddock and salmon beforehand and cooked the pie in the oven for 30 mins. I also used spring onion as well as white onion and it tasted AMAZING! Even my fussy child ate it along with my 10 month old.

Butter flour mixture ended up liquid. Will reduce the amount of butter next time. Total of 8 ounces of cheese went into mine for sauce and topping - supposedly extra sharp yet I could hardly taste it. I tried to spice up with coriander - a mistake - cayenne sounds a good idea. Used 10 oz fresh baby spinach, chopped, instead of frozen. Layering the potato over the sauce is tricky - I worked from the outside in with about a 3/4 inch layer. Difficult to avoid mixing potato with sauce - recommend to allow extra time for this. Pretty good but a fair amount of work - will try one more time before deciding whether it goes in the rotation.
We LOVE this dish! We have made it several times as is. Tonight we used mashed sweet potatoes instead of white. We also added shrimp and zucchini! Delicious!

Made if for my super picky kids and they loved it! I was able to sneak in fish and spinach’s and they had no idea! I also replaced the mashed potatoes with Idahoan instant potatoes so it was an even easier prep.

Enjoyed this fish recipe a lot! I adapted it to non-dairy by eliminating butter and using almond milk instead of cows milk. Divided between two dishes and used spinach in one and peas in the other. Good reception from the family, and will use soy milk next time! thanks!!

We made it with the spinach as in the recipe. It was very good. I used prepared mashed potatoes from the grocery store, which made it quicker. Perhaps the potatoes were already seasoned, but I added 1 tsp of salt and overall we all agreed we'd use less salt next time. But other than that, very tasty.
Follow suggested on reviews a little cayenne goes a long way/ brought out more, spicier on second day. Fantastic as leftovers as well
The recipe was easy to follow and turned out great.
This is very good comfort food. I did use frozen fillets and put mashed broccoli on top to cut the carbs. All those things were really wet! I will drain better next time, but the flavor was great!
I made this tonight & it was amazing. Very easy to cook & tasty.
Made it as instructed minus the spinach. Will definitely make it again
This was amazing! So full of flavor. This will definitely be added to our meal routine!
Lovely recipe. I also put in peas instead of the spinach and added in some cayenne pepper, and it turned out great.

Very good recipe,I switched up the spinach for sweet pea since my husband being English prefers it to spinach.
I have made this before without the onion and garlic this adds a nice flavour:)
